narrative: OMX30 opens in a precarious setup: technically in a bull regime (+3.5% above 200-MA) but operationally exhausted (-0.1% below 50-MA) with critically weak ADX (2.1). The global backdrop is decidedly risk-off—DAX, NASDAQ, and Nikkei all negative overnight—while VIX spiked +6.98%, signaling investor de-risking. US 10Y yields fell 111bp, typically a flight-to-safety signal that helps tech/growth but pressures bank NIM expansion. With RSI at 49.47 (neutral but near equilibrium), MACD above signal, and the index sitting 90% of 52-week range, there's no clear directional push. The Binance hack narrative adds tail-risk noise for fintech-exposed names. Expect choppy, range-bound trading with a mild downside bias.
morningBrief: OMX30 facing a confused setup on Friday morning: bulls can point to the +3.5% cushion above 200-MA and MACD still above signal, but bears have ADX at 2.1 (structurally weak), -0.1% slippage below 50-MA, and a sea of red globally (NASDAQ -138bp, DAX -56bp, Nikkei -212bp). VIX spike to 18.4 signals genuine de-risking. Key watch: hold 3123 (yesterday close) and 3100 technical support; resistance at 3145–3160 (50-MA zone) is heavy. Banks may see modest relief from yield decline if risk-off sentiment stabilizes, but industrials face headwinds from weak growth signals and continued commodity pressure (Brent -1.37%, copper -0.92%). Exporters (Volvo, Atlas, Ericsson) could pop on weaker SEK (USD/SEK -1.02%, EUR/SEK -0.66%), but NASDAQ weakness will dampen Hexagon and Ericsson sentiment. Avoid heroic longs; trade ranges and watch for a genuine trend setup. US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET is the only data event of note.
